headline.technical: Tech-led selloff hit Asia: TAIEX -6.03%, KOSPI -3.59%, Nikkei 225 -2.42% on 2026-11-16; FT reported Nvidia down 2.1% pre-market and WSJ the dollar index at a 19-month high of 103.533.
headline.layman: Tech and AI shares fell sharply in Asia on Monday, hitting Taiwan, South Korea and Japan hardest, while the US dollar got stronger.

global.title: AI-chip selloff and a firmer dollar weigh on markets

status.technical: Reuters, WSJ and FT describe an AI selloff with tech stocks under pressure before the US open; FT reported Nvidia down 2.1% pre-market. VIX closed at 19.97 (1d 3.47%). WSJ reported the DXY at a 19-month high of 103.533; US 10-year yield 5.15 on 2026-11-13.
status.layman: Tech and AI shares are under pressure at the start of a big week for AI. The dollar has strengthened. The VIX, a gauge of market nervousness, is at 19.97.

consequence.technical: If the exposure worries Reuters describes persist, further tech weakness is possible. The IMF's Georgieva warned circular financing among AI companies has grown to just over $1 trillion, two-thirds of it debt; Deutsche Bank warned markets may be underestimating rate hike risks (Investing.com).
consequence.layman: If worries about AI spending keep growing, tech shares could stay shaky. The IMF chief said money circling between AI firms is just over $1 trillion, two-thirds of it borrowed.

impact.technical: WSJ reported equal-weight funds held up better when Nvidia stumbled. NDTV Profit reported AMD, Micron, Intel and SanDisk down up to 5% pre-market. Yahoo Finance reported gold below $3,900 as Fed tightening expectations grew.
impact.layman: Chip makers fell before the US open, and gold slipped as investors expect the Fed to raise rates. Funds that spread money evenly across stocks coped better when Nvidia dropped, WSJ said.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary S&P 500 days the next day rose 54% of 846 times and the next 5 days rose 59% of 844 times; for the Nasdaq Composite, 55% of 825 and 59% of 823.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After calm days, the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of 846 times, and the Nasdaq Composite 55% of 825 times.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: chip names drag Taiwan, Korea and Japan

status.technical: TAIEX closed -6.03%, KOSPI -3.59% and Nikkei 225 -2.42% (1d). Hand-kept list: TSMC -5.74%, Hon Hai (Foxconn) -9.34%, Samsung Electronics -4.47%, SK Hynix -7.89%, Advantest -11.12%, Tokyo Electron -7.05% (1d).
status.layman: Stock markets in Taiwan, South Korea and Japan fell sharply on Monday. Big chip and electronics makers such as TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix were among the biggest fallers.

consequence.technical: NDTV Profit and FT reported chip stocks under pressure on AI jitters in pre-market US trading; if those worries persist, chip-heavy indices may stay exposed.
consequence.layman: Reports say AI worries are hitting chip shares. If those worries last, markets with many chip firms could stay bumpy.

impact.technical: WSJ reported Japan issued a verbal warning on the yen as weakness stokes intervention alert; USD/JPY closed at 159.64.
impact.layman: Japan warned in words about its weak yen, which investors read as a sign it could step in. The yen is trading near 159.64 per dollar.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 60% of 151 times for TAIEX, 54% of 153 for KOSPI and 55% of 163 for Nikkei 225.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After big one-day drops like this, the next day was up 60% of 151 times in Taiwan, 54% of 153 in Korea and 55% of 163 in Japan.

regions.title: Europe: small moves, UniCredit-Commerzbank bid cleared

status.technical: Euro Stoxx 50 -0.19%, DAX -0.13%, FTSE 100 0.24%, CAC 40 0.09% (1d on 2026-11-16). Euronews and WSJ reported EU approval of UniCredit's takeover of Commerzbank. WSJ reported eurozone industrial production rebounded in September.
status.layman: European stock markets barely moved. The EU approved UniCredit's takeover of Germany's Commerzbank, and factory output in the eurozone picked up in September.

consequence.technical: WSJ said the industrial sector has struggled to regain momentum amid persistently high energy costs driven by the war in Iran; if energy costs stay high, the recovery in industry may stay patchy.
consequence.layman: WSJ said high energy costs from the war in Iran have held factories back. If costs stay high, the recovery may stay uneven.

impact.technical: Bloomberg reported ECB Vice President Vujcic said AI and elevated public debt pose the biggest risks to euro zone financial stability. ECB main refinancing rate: 2.65 % for 2026-09-16.
impact.layman: A top ECB official said AI and high government debt are the biggest risks to Europe's financial system. The ECB's main lending rate is 2.65 %.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the next day rose 53% of 849 times for Euro Stoxx 50 and 55% of 865 for FTSE 100; the next 5 days rose 57% of 846 and 57% of 862 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After calm days, Euro Stoxx 50 rose the next day 53% of 849 times and the FTSE 100 55% of 865 times.

regions.title: Americas: US tech weak into Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO

status.technical: Latest US close (2026-11-13): S&P 500 -0.40%, Nasdaq Composite -0.91%, Dow 0.10%. FT and WSJ reported US tech set to open lower on Nvidia fallout. Hand-kept list: Nvidia -2.01% (1d), -12.75% (5d).
status.layman: On Friday the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell, and the Dow edged up. Reports say US tech shares were set to open lower on Monday after Nvidia's slide.

consequence.technical: WSJ said Nvidia reports earnings amid a leadership crisis and that Anthropic's IPO will test markets; if the results or the IPO disappoint, AI-linked shares could stay under pressure.
consequence.layman: Nvidia reports results this week during a leadership shake-up, and Anthropic may list its shares. Both are tests for AI stocks.

impact.technical: CNBC reported growing calls for Jensen Huang to return as Nvidia CEO following his resignation. Evidence on wider effects beyond tech is thin in the notes.
impact.layman: CNBC reported more people want Jensen Huang back as Nvidia's boss after he resigned. The notes say little about effects outside tech.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: for the Dow after ordinary days, the next day rose 52% of 853 times and the next 5 days rose 57% of 850 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After calm days, the Dow rose the next day 52% of 853 times.

drivers.title: Fed rate-hike expectations and a stronger dollar

status.technical: WSJ reported US Treasury yields declined but Fed rate-hike prospects remain in focus; Investing.com reported Deutsche Bank warned markets may be underestimating rate hike risks. DXY closed 103.52 (5d 1.84%); US 10-year yield 5.15.
status.layman: Investors are watching whether the Fed will raise interest rates. Deutsche Bank says markets may be underestimating that risk. The dollar has been getting stronger.

consequence.technical: SCMP reported gold is heading for its first annual loss in four years as concerns the Fed will raise rates spurred capital outflows; if hike expectations hold, dollar strength may persist.
consequence.layman: SCMP said gold may lose value for the year because investors fear the Fed will raise rates. If those fears hold, the dollar may stay strong.

impact.technical: Straits Times reported the Indonesian rupiah fell to a record low of 18,271 per dollar as Fed bets boosted the dollar; Reuters reported the South African rand slipped on the stronger dollar.
impact.layman: A stronger dollar is hurting other currencies. Indonesia's rupiah hit a record low, and South Africa's rand slipped.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the DXY rose the next day 51% of 825 times; the US 10-year yield rose 53% of 852 times and 55% of 850 times over the next 5 days.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After calm days, the dollar index was up the next day 51% of 825 times.

drivers.title: Oil: surplus forecasts versus Middle East threats

status.technical: WSJ reported oil fell Monday, reversing initial gains, as traders weighed signs of a global supply surplus against renewed threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments. Brent closed 95.22 (1d -0.65%).
status.layman: Oil prices fell on Monday. Traders weighed signs of too much oil supply against new threats to Middle East shipping.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported Goldman Sachs sees a "sizable" 2027 surplus and expects Brent to average $88 a barrel next year, easing to $78 by year-end; Bloomberg also reported Iran launched drones at a US site at Riffa base in Bahrain while saying a path to ending the conflict remains open.
consequence.layman: Goldman Sachs expects oil to get cheaper next year because there will be extra supply. Iran also attacked a base in Bahrain but says talks remain possible.

impact.technical: WSJ said high energy costs from the war in Iran weigh on eurozone industry; Reuters reported India's wholesale inflation accelerated to 12.29% in October on a fuel price surge.
impact.layman: High fuel costs are squeezing European factories and pushing up prices in India, where wholesale inflation hit 12.29% in October.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days Brent rose the next day 53% of 847 times and the next 5 days 51% of 844 times; look-alike days saw a 5-day rise 0 of 5 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After calm days, Brent was up the next day 53% of 847 times.

status.technical: Reuters reported an AI selloff has investors scrambling to measure their true exposure. IMF's Georgieva said circular financing among AI companies is just over $1 trillion, two-thirds of it debt (CNBC). ECB's Vujcic named AI and elevated public debt as the biggest euro zone financial stability risks (Bloomberg).
status.layman: Investors are worried about how much they depend on AI companies. The IMF chief said AI firms financing each other has reached just over $1 trillion, mostly debt.

consequence.technical: WSJ said Anthropic's mega-IPO will test markets; if enthusiasm for AI keeps cooling, as the IMF chief described, heavily indebted AI projects could look more vulnerable.
consequence.layman: If excitement about AI keeps cooling, companies that borrowed heavily for AI projects could look riskier.

impact.technical: WSJ commentary said AI players that bet heavily on a handful of mega data-centre projects look vulnerable after the midterm elections. Morningstar noted UK trusts with Anthropic exposure.
impact.layman: A WSJ column said AI firms relying on a few giant data-centre projects look vulnerable. Evidence on who else is affected is thin.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: for the Nasdaq Composite, look-alike days saw the next 5 days rise 3 of 5 times (median 0.64%) and the next 21 days rise 3 of 5 times (median 0.31%).
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. In 5 similar past cases, the Nasdaq Composite was higher 5 days later in 3 of them.

drivers.title: China-US diplomacy: Xi-Trump-Putin summit and APEC

status.technical: CNBC reported China confirmed a Xi-Trump-Putin summit, expected to cover nuclear non-proliferation, the Middle East war, trade policies and possibly Ukraine. Bloomberg said Shenzhen hosts APEC this week. Shenzhen Component closed -2.53% (1d); Shanghai Composite -0.87%.
status.layman: China confirmed a summit of the leaders of China, the US and Russia. China's stock markets fell on Monday, Shenzhen by 2.53%.

consequence.technical: CNBC reported Senator Cantwell urged Commerce Secretary Lutnick to stop AI chip sales to China ahead of the Xi meeting; Euronews reported Canada's PM Carney said Canada is ready to turn to Chinese carmakers if US trade talks fail.
consequence.layman: A US senator wants AI chip sales to China stopped before the meeting. Canada says it could turn to Chinese carmakers if US trade talks fail.

impact.technical: SCMP reported Goldman Sachs upgraded Hong Kong-listed Chinese stocks to overweight for 2027 and downgraded A shares, while Morgan Stanley diverged.
impact.layman: Goldman Sachs now prefers Chinese shares listed in Hong Kong over those on the mainland for 2027. Morgan Stanley disagrees.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, the Shenzhen Component's next day rose 49% of 168 times; for the Hang Seng after ordinary days, 49% of 816 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After big drops, Shenzhen was up the next day 49% of 168 times.

drivers.title: India: rupee firm, benchmarks higher, rate-hike worry

status.technical: Business Standard reported Sensex ended 512 pts higher and Nifty at 25,291; market data show Sensex 0.63% and Nifty 50 0.58% (1d). Economic Times reported the rupee closed 0.3% higher at 93.9225 per dollar, with November foreign equity inflows of nearly $10 billion.
status.layman: Indian share markets rose on Monday and the rupee strengthened. Foreign investors have put in nearly $10 billion in November.

consequence.technical: Mint reported Indian benchmarks fell Friday as higher-than-expected retail inflation raised concerns about a possible RBI rate hike; if inflation stays high, those concerns may return.
consequence.layman: Higher-than-expected inflation made investors worry the RBI could raise rates. If inflation stays high, that worry may come back.

impact.technical: Business Standard reported Morgan Stanley expects the Sensex may rise 16% by December 2027 on an earnings recovery (a forecast attributed to the bank, not a certainty).
impact.layman: Morgan Stanley thinks the Sensex could rise 16% by December 2027. That is the bank's opinion, not a sure thing.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Nifty 50 rose the next day 52% of 847 times; look-alike days saw the next 21 days rise 1 of 5 times (median -4.95%).
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After calm days, the Nifty 50 rose the next day 52% of 847 times.

events.technical: WSJ and Investing.com say Nvidia reports amid a leadership crisis, a key test for AI-linked stocks.
events.layman: Nvidia reports its results this week. It is a big test for AI shares.

events.title: Anthropic IPO in focus
events.technical: WSJ and Investing.com say Anthropic's mega-IPO will test markets; the notes give no date.
events.layman: Anthropic may list its shares, which will test how much investors want AI.

events.technical: Mint reports the Rs 8,981-crore offer for sale by Coal India opens November 19; investors watch dividend prospects.
events.layman: A Coal India subsidiary starts selling shares to the public on November 19.

events.title: APEC hosted in Shenzhen
events.technical: Bloomberg says Shenzhen hosts APEC this week; Canada's PM Carney plans to meet Xi there, with autos on the agenda (Euronews).
events.layman: Leaders meet in Shenzhen this week; trade and cars are on the agenda.

events.title: Asean leaders summit in Manila
events.technical: Bloomberg reports Asean kicked off a three-day leaders summit in Manila, attended by India's Modi.
events.layman: Southeast Asian leaders are meeting in Manila for three days.

companyEffects.technical: FT reported Nvidia down 2.1% pre-market on AI jitters; CNBC reported growing calls for Jensen Huang's return following his resignation.
companyEffects.layman: Nvidia shares fell 2.1% before the US open, and people want its former boss back after he resigned.
